Recently, variable stepsize semi-implicit semi-implicit methods (SDIMSIMs) have been introduced, and these methods have been shown to effectively handle stiff problems with changing step sizes. However, there was no prior research on developing variable stepsize SDIMSIMs. This study introduces two types of variable stepsize methods within the framework of SDIMs and DIMSIMs, and demonstrates their accuracy through numerical experiments, including a case where they outperform traditional fixed stepsize methods.

This paper introduces a multivariate functional singular spectrum analysis (MFSSA) method,
which is an extension of multivariate singular spectrum analysis (MSSA) and accounts for
functions defined over continuous domains. We provide a detailed examination of the
algorithms used in the MSSA and discuss the benefits of utilizing discrete versions of
functions in the multivariate FSSA. A thorough assessment of the multivariate FSSA
methodology is conducted through both simulated and real-world data sets, which
consist of multivariate versions of the German weather data set and the multivariate
FSSA's ability to forecast future data points is also evaluated.

Recent studies have shown that adversarial examples can easily be created against state-of-the-art audio recognition systems, yet the underlying reason for their vulnerability remains unclear. This study proposes that deep neural network-based audio recognition systems are prone to overfitting on spurious correlations, leading to overreactive behavior and overstable states. We introduce the concepts of overstable and overreactive to explain the susceptibility of these systems to adversarial attacks. We further propose a novel metric, the Audio Reactivity Score (ARS), to quantify the overreactive nature of audio recognition systems. We also introduce the Audio Stability Score (ASS) to measure the overstable states of these systems. We demonstrate that both ARS and ASS are effective indicators of a system's susceptibility to adversarial attacks. We also show that both scores are negatively correlated with adversarial robustness. We also show that both scores are capable of ranking the robustness of audio recognition systems against existing adversarial attacks. We also show that both scores can be used to identify the weak points of audio recognition systems. We also propose two novel defenses, the Audio Stability Augmentation (ASA) and the Audio Reactivity Optimization (ARO), to enhance the robustness of audio recognition systems. We demonstrate that both defenses are effective in improving the robustness of audio recognition systems against existing adversarial attacks.

This study focuses on the behavior of a one-dimensional random walk, denoted as $S_n$, with $n$ steps. The expected time for the walk to spend in a specific interval, $a$ to $b$, during its first visit to $0$ is represented by local time, denoted as $L_n^{[a,b]}$. Our research reveals that for random walks starting at $0$, there exists a non-zero probability that the walk will never visit $0$ again after spending time in the interval $[a,b]$ during its initial visit to $0$. This phenomenon is quantified by the probability measure $\mathbb{P}_0\big(L_{n}^{[a,b]} > 0 \text{ for all } n \geq 1\big)$. We derive an exact formula for this probability, which is equal to the ratio of the product of the distances from $0$ to the nearest points in $[a,b]$ to the product of all possible distances from $0$ to points in $(a,b)$. This research builds upon a recent finding by Demaine and Shlosman, which established a similar but less precise bound for the probability.

The IShTAR test facility in Italy is designed to investigate ionized plasma interactions with materials in the context of fusion devices.  To achieve this, the facility utilizes a helicon plasma source that can produce high-density plasma at low temperatures.  This source is based on a modified version of the EXPLOR device, which has been upgraded to include the helicon mode of operation.  In order to validate the performance of the source, the paper presents an analysis of the plasma characteristics, which were measured using various diagnostic tools.  The results show that the source is capable of producing a plasma density of up to 1.5 x 10^12 m^-3, which is consistent with theoretical predictions.  The results also show that the source can be controlled to produce a plasma with a temperature of up to 10 eV, which is suitable for a range of experiments.  The paper concludes that the source is performing as expected and is ready to be used for a range of experiments.

This research examines a microbial pesticide model that includes a suppression mechanism, which is controlled by an external factor. We analyze the model's stability and sensitivity, taking into account varying levels of control. A model that incorporates seasonal changes in microbial growth is also developed and compared to a non-seasonal model. Finally, we take a numerical approach to illustrate the impact of control on the model's dynamics.

This study introduces a novel nucleus segmentation framework, which combines a two-stage approach and a small object detection strategy. The proposed histopathology image nucleus segmentation framework is comprised of two primary stages: nucleus identification and nucleus segmentation. The first stage, nucleus identification, is designed to identify and extract the nuclei of interest from the input image, while the second stage, nucleus segmentation, is designed to segment each nucleus into its corresponding sub-regions. The proposed framework is comprised of two primary modules, which are the W-Net identification module and the W-Net segmentation module. The W-Net identification module is designed to identify and extract the nuclei of interest from the input image, while the W-Net segmentation module is designed to segment each nucleus into its corresponding sub-regions. The proposed framework is comprised of several innovative techniques, which are the use of a histopathology image preprocessing technique, the use of a multi-scale feature fusion technique, and the use of a multi-scale feature fusion technique. The proposed framework is designed to address the challenges associated with nucleus segmentation in histopathology images, which are the small object detection challenge, the nucleus touching challenge, and the nucleus shape irregularity challenge. The proposed framework is evaluated on three publicly available datasets, which are the PANDA, the CAMEO, and the PanNuke datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of nucleus segmentation accuracy.

In the context of finite classical groups, the local exchange theorem for special orthogonal and symplectic types has been established for characteristic not equal to two. This study extends that knowledge by proving the local exchange theorem for special orthogonal and symplectic groups in positive characteristic.

Xia and Zhang in 2014 introduced the concept of a hamiltonian path index for a graph G, which is the minimum number k needed to add to G so that its k-times repeated line graph has a hamiltonian path. In this study, we first explore graphs with a repeated line graph of order k that is hamiltonian, and then determine the hamiltonian path index for several graph types, including snarks, complete bipartite graphs K_{n,n}, and wheel graphs W_n.

Pyroptosis, a highly inflammatory cell death process, is triggered by the SARS-CoV-2 virus and is linked to the cytokine storm that is associated with severe cases.  To gain a deeper understanding of pyroptosis, we developed a mathematical model that incorporates the interactions between SARS-CoV-2, immune cells, inflammatory cytokines, and gasdermin D, a key molecule in pyroptosis.  Our model was calibrated using data from human cell cultures and simulations revealed that pyroptosis is initiated by the virus's protease, which activates gasdermin D.  We also found that the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein can directly stimulate gasdermin D through a process called endocytosis.  Additionally, our model showed that the production of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1β is dependent on the activation of gasdermin D, and that IL-1β can further promote pyroptosis in a feedback loop.  To explore the effects of anti-inflammatory treatments, our model simulated the effects of IL-1 receptor antagonists and caspase-1 inhibitors, and found that they can reduce pyroptosis and the production of IL-1β.  These findings suggest that pyroptosis may play a significant role in the cytokine storm associated with severe cases of COVID-19, and that targeting pyroptosis may be a promising therapeutic strategy.

We investigate the impact of external state variables and rewards on learning in reinforcement learning. We find that including irrelevant external state variables and rewards can hinder learning, even when the core task remains unchanged. We develop a method to identify and eliminate irrelevant external state variables and rewards, and demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments on multiple tasks.

This paper introduces HELMHOLTZ, a refinement type validator for Tezos smart contracts, which addresses the growing demand for formal verification in this emerging blockchain technology.  As one of the first platforms to integrate on-chain refinement types, Tezos enables developers to write code with static guarantees, which can be further enhanced by a formal specification using a language like Coq.  Our work builds on the existing OCaml-based Tezos development framework and the Refinement Type System for OCaml (RETOCAML), which allows for the validation of refined types and ensures that code can be ported to the Tezos blockchain with minimal changes.  Experimental results show that HELMHOLTZ can successfully validate complex data structures, including maps and lists, and that the resulting code is both efficient and easy to optimize.

This study introduces a novel, intuitive interpretation of graph convolutional neural networks (GCNNs) through the lens of matched filtering, a fundamental signal processing technique. By leveraging this interpretation, we introduce a novel GCNN architecture that integrates the filtering technique with a pointwise nonlinearity, enabling the network to adaptively learn optimal filters. Notably, our approach can be applied to both node and graph-level tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our GCNN outperforms existing methods on node classification benchmarks, achieving an accuracy of 89.1% on the Cora dataset and 84.5% on the Citeseer dataset. Furthermore, our GCNN achieves a performance of 79.1% in graph-level task and 84.5% in node classification task.

We develop a Chern-Simons-like action for a complex scalar field in curved spacetime, which is gauge invariant and includes the Wess-Zumino term. By applying the Hamiltonian formalism, we derive the corresponding bulk Chern-Simons-Gross-Neveu equations of motion. In a specific gauge, we find that this action is equivalent to the standard Hamiltonian gravity-hair action. We then examine the properties of stationary solutions, including black holes and solitons, in the Chern-Simons-HG model. We also compare the Chern-Simons and standard Hamiltonian descriptions of these solutions, focusing on their conserved charges and thermodynamic behavior.

We've identified a class of theories in 4+2 dimensions that exhibit Kdumov-type duality, featuring an odd number of spatial dimensions, and have discovered that this duality can be understood through the exchange of an SU(2) symmetry and a U(1) magnetic moment, facilitated by a stack of three-branes.

In ultrasound elastography, determining the lateral shift of tissue accurately is crucial for generating high-quality images. However, conventional methods for estimating this shift are limited by the effects of ultrasound beamforming on the received signals. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach called Virtual Source Synthetic Aperture (VSSA) that utilizes beamformed data to estimate shift in both lateral and elevation directions. By employing a beamformed delay-and-sum (DAS) reference image, VSSA compensates for the effects of beamforming and provides more accurate shift estimation. Our results demonstrate that VSSA outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and resolution, with a significant improvement in peak correlation width. Furthermore, VSSA enables the creation of strain images with enhanced resolution and reduced noise, with a significant improvement in peak strain width. Overall, VSSA represents a significant advancement in the field of ultrasound elastography and has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy.

This paper introduces the concept of Logical Pseudocode, a novel approach to
algorithms that integrates algorithms with invariants and proofs through
first-order logic, effectively bridging the gap between these two areas. As a
result, Logical Pseudocode enables us to develop a range of algorithms,
including the all-nearest neighbors algorithm for the metric space clustering
problem, and a distributed algorithm for finding the maximum weight edge in a
graph. By utilizing Logical Pseudocode, we can verify the correctness of these
algorithms and ensure their robustness.

A key question in Boolean Ramsey theory is finding the minimum height $n$ of elements in the Boolean lattice $\mathcal{P}(k)$, where any $r$-coloring of the lattice elements ensures a monochromatic object of a specific type. We've determined the minimum height $n$ needed to guarantee a monochromatic $p$-shaped poset for any number of colors $r$ and size $k$. We also found the minimum height for a monochromatic $V$ with any number of branches for any number of colors $r$ and branch size $k$, as well as a general formula for $V$ with any number of branches.

In the context of online learning with expert advice, we examine the problem of dynamic clustering, where a stream of points in a metric space is processed, and for each point, a cost is incurred based on selecting a center that minimizes the point's distance. Newcomer points can trigger the addition of new centers, with a limit of $k$ centers. We develop an algorithm for high-dimensional spaces that incurs a cost of $O(k^{2/3}k_\tau^{1/3}(d+\log k)^{1/3})$ times the optimal cost, with $k_\tau$ being the new stream's size and $d$ being the space's dimension.

We develop a hierarchical approach to resolve finite horizon, discrete-time, deterministic, zero-sum, stochastic chase-evasion games that occur in $\mathbb{R}^d$. This approach involves breaking down the complex $d$-dimensional game into simpler, independent one-dimensional games that take place at various times and in different spatial locations. Each of these lower-dimensional games is then assigned a decision maker based on their ability to influence the game's outcome. We demonstrate that this hierarchical arrangement is equivalent to the original game and can be used to derive a closed-form solution for the game's value function.

Consider a probability space consisting of events A, B, and C. We can define a cyclic likelihood, where the probability of event A occurring given that both B and C have occurred is greater than the probability of event B occurring given that both A and C have occurred, which in turn is greater than the probability of event C occurring given that both A and B have occurred. We can also define a nontransitive likelihood, where the probability of event A occurring given that both B and C have occurred is less than the probability of event B occurring given that both A and C have occurred, which in turn is less than the probability of event C occurring given that both A and B have occurred. Although it is well-known that conditional probability does not always follow the rule that if P(A|B) is greater than P(B|A), then P(B|C) must be greater than P(C|B), we can show that both nontransitive and cyclic likelihoods can be achieved through the manipulation of conditional probabilities.

Restoring low-dose CT images is crucial for reducing patient radiation exposure and improving image quality.  Deep learning techniques have been particularly successful in restoring these images, with various models achieving impressive results.  However, the performance of these models can be hindered by the need for them to process each image pixel by pixel, which can be time-consuming and computationally expensive.  In this paper, we propose a new approach called AdaIN-Switchable CycleGAN, which utilizes a switchable architecture to bypass the need for pixel-wise processing.  Our model leverages adversarial training to learn a mapping between low-dose and normal-dose CT images, while also employing AdaSwitch to adaptively switch between different network branches.  Our approach has been shown to outperform existing models in terms of both image quality and computational efficiency, with a significant reduction in training time and a notable improvement in PSNR and SSIM scores.

Recent advancements in dialog understanding have been driven by the development of multi-task learning and semi-supervised contrastive pre-training.
To address the limitations of these approaches, we introduce a comprehensive framework that combines semi-supervised contrastive pre-training with a tree-structured architecture.
This framework, named SPACE-2, utilizes a semi-Markov logic network to model dialog semantics and employs contrastive pre-training to enhance the learning of unannotated utterances.
Our experiments on the MultiWOZ 2.0 dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of joint task accuracy and end-to-end accuracy, achieving a significant improvement of 4.1% in joint task accuracy and 3.6% in end-to-end accuracy.

This research paper focuses on a specific type of soliton, the conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton, and examines its implications within ideal fluid spacetime. By analyzing the geometric structure of this spacetime, we demonstrate that it is not compatible with the said soliton. Additionally, we establish that a perfect fluid with this soliton must exhibit either a timelike or spacelike Killing vector field.

We have investigated the rotational characteristics of rotating distorted halo nuclei by applying the cranked relativistic mean field model to four specific isotopes - $^{11}$Li, $^{19}$C, $^{22}$Na, and $^{26}$Mg - in the ground state and states with angular momentum greater than zero. Our study reveals that the neutron halo in $^{11}$Li is significantly influenced by the rotation, while the shape of $^{19}$C changes from an oblate to a prolate configuration as a result of the rotational force. The addition of angular momentum in $^{22}$Na results in the expansion of the neutron halo, while the rotation in $^{26}$Mg leads to the formation of a double halo structure. Our study also highlights the concept of shape decoupling effects, where the rotation of a nucleus can lead to the formation of a new structure in the inner core, resulting in the appearance of a halo in the outer halo.

This paper introduces an advanced version of the video super-resolution model, BasicVSR, referred to as BasicVSR++, which incorporates two key enhancements over the original version. Firstly, the recurrent propagation process in BasicVSR++ is modified to employ a large kernel convolution, which effectively captures long-range temporal dependencies and significantly boosts performance. Secondly, the temporal alignment process in BasicVSR++ is improved by utilizing a large kernel convolution, which outperforms the original small kernel convolution used in BasicVSR. Notably, the proposed large kernel convolution can be seamlessly integrated into the video super-resolution framework without requiring additional model parameters or computational costs. Experimental results demonstrate that BasicVSR++ achieves superior video super-resolution performance compared to the original BasicVSR model.

This research focuses on the precision of next-to-leading order (NLO) QCD calculations for the dominant vector boson fusion (VBF) production of Higgs bosons and electroweak production of weak boson scattering (WBS) processes at a future muon collider. We examine the impact of higher-order QCD corrections and uncertainties in parton distribution functions (PDFs) on these processes. We also investigate the potential for NLO QCD predictions to be used in a likelihood fit for the measurement of the VBF/WBS cross-sections. We find that NLO QCD corrections significantly affect the shape of the final state, particularly in the case of the VBF process, and that PDF uncertainties have a notable impact on the measurement. We also find that the NLO QCD predictions are accurate enough to be used in a likelihood fit, and that the statistical uncertainty in the measurement is dominated by the systematic uncertainty in the PDF.

In multi-task reinforcement learning, a single learned policy is adapted to
address various tasks, with two primary approaches: either separate models are
created for each task or a single model is used to learn from multiple tasks,
with the latter being more efficient but prone to catastrophic interference.
We introduce a novel architecture called Modular Networks that utilizes task-
specific subnetworks to model task-specific relationships, with a novel loss
function that prevents catastrophic interference by preventing information
sharing between subnetworks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this
architecture in multi-task reinforcement learning, with experiments on two
benchmark environments, showing that it achieves superior performance compared
to alternative approaches.

This paper provides new upper bound estimates for the gradient of weak solutions to a specific type of nonlinear parabolic equation, defined on a complete, non-compact metric measure space with compact boundary. The underlying space has a Ricci curvature that decreases over time and a measure that expands at a certain rate. We also derive similar estimates for the fast diffusion type equation under these conditions.

This talk will present an updated version of Godel's Incompleteness Theorem that surpasses all previous iterations, including those by Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser. We will also provide a direct proof of the Incompleteness Theorem, which does not rely on the diagonal lemma, and discuss the limitations of formal axiomatic systems in capturing essential properties of natural numbers.

This study extends the classical three balls conjecture to functions in Clifford analysis, specifically focusing on monogenic functions. We establish an inequality that relates the norm of a monogenic function to its derivative and value within two overlapping balls, and subsequently derive an exponential growth estimate for the function in a third ball based on this inequality.

This paper introduces a novel approach to sampling from a population, taking into account both spatial distribution and equity. Our method, the Sequential Spatially Equitable Sampling (SSES), builds on previous work and allows for the selection of a sample that is representative of the population in both aspects. The SSES algorithm is designed to be sequential, allowing for the selection of the sample in stages, and is shown to be effective in a variety of settings through a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.

Calibrating an eye-controlled camera is essential for accurate performance of robot tasks, and while traditional methods exist, they are costly and time-consuming. A new approach is proposed that utilizes machine learning to calibrate the camera from a single image, but this method's reliance on unlabelled data makes it susceptible to incorrect results. A more effective solution is proposed that combines a small set of carefully chosen images with an eye-controlled camera to improve the method's performance and reduce the need for a large dataset.

In solving inverse problems, we aim to recover an unknown input from a given observation. This task is often ill-posed, meaning that multiple solutions can fit the data equally well. To address this, we incorporate prior knowledge about the unknown input into our estimation process. This is typically done using Bayesian inference, which allows us to estimate the entire posterior distribution of the unknown input. This is crucial for understanding the reliability of our solution and for propagating uncertainty to downstream applications. However, estimating the entire posterior distribution is a computationally expensive process, and traditional methods like Markov Chain Monte Carlo can be too slow. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to efficiently estimate the posterior distribution by using a modified version of the Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN). Our method is based on a regularized version of the Mean-Field Variational Approximation, which we show can be optimized using a gradient-based approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on two different inverse problems: image deblurring and compressed sensing.

This note examines the possibility of invariant surfaces in dynamical systems where the vector field is defined by a fractional order derivative. We demonstrate that there are no equivalent surfaces in this type of system under the assumption of a smooth, time-dependent transformation that preserves the surface's structure over time.

Next-generation wireless networks will utilize terahertz (THz) frequency bands to achieve ultra-high data transfer rates, but the short reach of THz signals necessitates the development of multi-hop communication systems.  In these systems, beam training is crucial for establishing reliable connections between devices, but traditional methods that rely on a two-hop setup are limited.  In this paper, we investigate the challenges of enhancing beam training in a multi-hop THz communication system, specifically focusing on a linear multi-hop scenario.  We propose a novel approach that utilizes a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm to optimize the beam training process, allowing for more efficient and reliable connections between devices.  Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing significant improvements in beam training performance compared to traditional methods.

A new method has been developed to study the interstellar medium by analyzing scintillation patterns in radio signals from pulsars. This technique focuses on the phase patterns of scintillation and can detect small changes in the scintillation pattern caused by density fluctuations in the interstellar medium. By using this method, researchers can probe the properties of the radio waves as they travel through the interstellar medium and can potentially detect the effects of the Galactic magnetic field on the scintillation pattern. A study applying this method to the pulsar B133+16 found that the scintillation pattern changes over time and that these changes can be used to probe the properties of the interstellar medium. The results of this study suggest that the interstellar medium is affected by the Galactic magnetic field and that this effect can be detected through scintillometry.

To generate high-quality speech, neural network models have been extensively studied, and the recent WaveNet architecture has shown promising results. However, WaveNet's slow inference speed and lack of interpretability hinder its practical use. In this study, we introduce Quasi-Periodic WaveNet, a novel model that combines the strengths of Wavenet and human speech production mechanisms. Our model uses a pitch-dependent expanded convolution neural network to capture the periodic characteristics of speech, while a non-periodic network captures the speech content. We also introduce an adaptive filter that dynamically adjusts to the varying pitch periods. Our model achieves a significant improvement in generation speed compared to WaveNet, while maintaining high generation quality. Our Quasi-Periodic WaveNet outperforms the state-of-the-art pitch-synchronous speech generation models in both objective and subjective evaluations.

This study introduces MADARi, a comprehensive web platform designed for annotating and correcting Arabic text at a character level.  The site is specifically tailored for NLP tasks in low-resource languages, with an emphasis on Semitic languages such as Arabic, Hebrew, and Aramaic.  By integrating a range of pre-built annotation tools, MADARi streamlines the process of adding sub-word and morphological information to text, which is particularly beneficial for tasks like tokenization, morphological analysis, and part-of-speech tagging.  The site is user-friendly, with a built-in error detection system that highlights common spelling errors and suggests corrections, thus speeding up the annotation process.  By making the annotation process more efficient, MADARi accelerates the creation of high-quality annotated datasets, which are essential for training and evaluating NLP models.  The site is open-source and freely available for use, with its code hosted on GitHub.

This study examines the photochemistry and spectral properties of temperate terrestrial exoplanets, focusing on their atmospheric composition and spectral characteristics. The research highlights the importance of understanding these properties to accurately assess the potential habitability of exoplanets. The study also emphasizes the need for further characterization of gas-rich exoplanets to gain a more comprehensive understanding of their atmospheres. The research is presented in a visually intuitive manner, utilizing a series of visual aids to convey key concepts and findings. The study is particularly relevant to upcoming space missions designed to explore and characterize exoplanets.

The search for topological superconductivity in hybrid semiconductor-superconductor nanowires has been hindered by the difficulty in differentiating the zero-bias peak associated with Majorana fermions from other peaks caused by impurities or other mechanisms. A promising direction for resolving this issue lies in investigating the tunneling environment surrounding the nanowire. This study explores the impact of an Ohmic environment on the topological properties of a semiconductor nanowire and reveals that the energy spectrum of the system is significantly altered by the environment, with the Majorana mode exhibiting unique spectral broadening and a distinct peak shape compared to other modes. These findings suggest that tunneling spectroscopy with resistive electrodes can be used to distinguish the Majorana peak from other peaks, with the peak shape and width serving as key indicators of the system's topological properties.

This project, RoadAtlas, is an advanced system designed to automatically identify road defects and manage infrastructure using cutting-edge technology. By utilizing computer vision and machine learning, the system can detect various road issues such as cracks, potholes, and other defects, and generate detailed reports for maintenance purposes. The project leverages the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm and Python for image processing, and can be accessed through a web interface built with Flask and HTML. The system is capable of processing images from various sources, including drones and static cameras, and can be easily integrated with existing infrastructure management systems. The project aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of road flaw detection and asset management, and can be easily adapted for use in a variety of settings.

This paper introduces a bicategorical definition of shadows, which goes beyond the previously known categorical framework. We demonstrate that key concepts such as idempotents, separable functors, and Frobenius functors can be expressed in terms of shadows within the bicategorical framework.

Localizing images is a challenging task, particularly when it comes to identifying and isolating objects of interest.  In this paper, we introduce a new dataset called LVND, which consists of 100k images that contain multiple objects marked with various types of noise.  We explore the limits of current object localization techniques by testing them on this dataset.  Our experiments show that even the most advanced models struggle to achieve high performance on this dataset, with the best results falling short of 50% mIoU.  To address this challenge, we introduce a new benchmark for object localization in visually complex scenes.

We introduce a new type of graph neural network called Lorentzian GNNs, which are based on a hyperbolic space known as the Lorentzian manifold. This allows for the representation of graphs in a space that models spacetime, providing a more accurate representation of real-world data. We show that Lorentzian GNNs can be used to perform a variety of graph-based tasks, including node classification and link prediction, and we demonstrate their effectiveness through a series of experiments.

This research addresses an inverse problem where the goal is to identify a moving boundary in a solid object based on sound pressure measurements taken in the surrounding fluid. The problem involves determining the shape of the object's surface, which is in motion, from acoustic data. We develop a new approach to this problem by using a specific mathematical model that accounts for the interaction between the solid and fluid, known as fluid-structure interaction (FSI). The FSI model is based on the Navier-Stokes and acoustic equations, which describe the behavior of the solid and fluid, respectively. The research also establishes a connection between the FSI model and a new mathematical problem that involves only the fluid. This reformulation is crucial for developing an efficient numerical method to solve the inverse problem. The new approach uses a level set function to represent the moving boundary and employs a specific numerical method, known as the Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) method, to solve the reformulated problem. The method is tested on a simple example, which demonstrates its effectiveness in identifying the moving boundary. The research contributes to the development of advanced imaging techniques, such as ultrasound, which use sound waves to create images of moving objects.

In optical compression transfer, a change in the frequency of light is achieved through interaction with a mechanical oscillator. This technique is typically used to generate entangled photon pairs, but its application in creating steady-state hybrid entanglement between light and sound has not been fully explored. This research investigates the dynamics of a hybrid light-matter system, where a qubit is entangled with an optomechanical system through photon emission and mechanical vibrations. By analyzing the system's behavior under different conditions, researchers found that compression transfer can lead to the creation of hybrid entanglement in a short amount of time. This entanglement can be maintained for a significant period, even in the presence of various types of dissipation. The research also reveals that the presence of a mechanical bath can actually enhance the lifetime of entanglement, a phenomenon that has not been observed in previous studies. These findings suggest that optical compression transfer may be a useful tool for controlling and maintaining hybrid entanglement in the future.

This paper introduces the entity-based $\Sigma$-m$\mu$calculus, a variant of the tree-based m$\mu$calculus that incorporates additional operators for the least and greatest fixed points of entity-based formulas. We examine the properties of the entity-based m$\mu$calculus, including its relationship to the modal $\mu$-calculus and the modal fixed-point logic, and provide a parsimonious parity game characterization for the evaluation of formulas. We also present a characterization of the m$\mu$calculus through a game-theoretic approach.

This study introduces a novel exponential discounting model within the framework of Tsallis psychology, addressing key issues such as time inconsistency, hyperbolic behavior, and dual-system dynamics. By deriving key properties and applying a utility maximization approach, we demonstrate the model's capacity to explain complex decision-making patterns, including switching behavior and concrete real-world scenarios. Furthermore, we establish a direct relationship between the Tsallis and hyperbolic models, highlighting the versatility and broader applicability of the Tsallis model.

We examine the possibility of establishing a harmonic gauge in the newly proposed hefty gravity theory, which is a harmonic gauge equivalent to a specific choice of the Lagrange multiplier in hefty gravity. However, we find that this equivalence only holds true in linearized theory, and cannot be realized in the full nonlinear context of hefty gravity.

A signed graph is created by overlaying a signing on an existing graph. The concept of homomorphism for signed graphs was first introduced by Erdos and Nešetřil in 1984 as a theoretical limit for expanding the connections of a given signed graph. In 2014, the idea of double covers for signed graphs was proposed, which could potentially have an expansion factor of at least two. In this paper, we explore the connection between expanded double covers and the notion of homomorphism for signed graphs, which leads to a proof that any graph with a particular type of symmetry can be mapped onto a given signed graph with a particular property. This proof also results in an affirmative answer to a question posed by Postle and Schaefer in 2014, which states that any graph with a particular type of symmetry can be mapped onto a given signed graph with an expanded double cover factor of at least $2k$ for any positive integer $k$.

This article examines the Weyl-Wigner representation of canonical equilibrium states within the framework of canonical quantum statistics. It specifically investigates the Wigner function and related quantities, such as the Weyl symbol, for both non-interacting and interacting systems. The article also provides a practical example using the harmonic oscillator and the RPA approximation for an interacting system.

This paper provides a critical analysis of the concept of negative absolute temperature, which has been the subject of debate in recent years. We argue that the controversy surrounding negative absolute temperature stems from an incomplete understanding of the statistical mechanics formula used to describe the entropy of a two-level system. By examining the limitations of the Boltzmann entropy expression, we demonstrate that, under specific conditions, a system can exhibit an entropy that increases with decreasing temperature, even down to negative values. These conditions, however, are not commonly met in practice, as they require a system with a bounded phase space and a specific relationship between its energy levels. We further explore the implications of our findings, which suggest that the concept of negative absolute temperature may be more theoretical than practical, and that it is unlikely to be observed in real-world systems.

Let G be an abelian group and let A and B be non-empty subsets of G. For any positive integer s, we define the restricted s-fold signed sumset of A as follows:
$$
s\hat{+}A = \{a_1 + \cdots + a_s : a_1, \ldots, a_s \in A\}
$$
and similarly, we define the restricted s-fold signed sumset of the Cartesian product of A and B as:
$$
s\hat{+}(A \times B) = \{(a_1 + \cdots + a_s, b_1 + \cdots + b_s) : (a_i, b_i) \in A \times B, i = 1, \ldots, s\}
$$
In this paper, we investigate the structure of the restricted s-fold signed sumsets of integers and demonstrate that if A and B are finite subsets of integers with sufficiently large difference between their cardinality and maximum element, then A must be a finite union of arithmetic progressions with the same common difference as B, and B must be a finite union of intervals. Additionally, we establish a Cauchy-Davenport-type theorem for the structure of the restricted s-fold signed sumset of integers, and establish a structure for A if the cardinality of s-fold signed sumset of A is less than or equal to the cardinality of s-fold signed sum

The detection and classification of colorectal polyps in histopathological images is a crucial step in preventing colorectal cancer.  However, the lack of annotated histopathological datasets hinders the development of automated classification systems.  To address this issue, we have created UniToPatho, a comprehensive and publicly available dataset containing 1,000 histopathological images of colorectal polyps, annotated with classification and adenoma abnormality grading labels.  The dataset was created to facilitate the development of automated systems for polyp classification and abnormality grading.  To evaluate the effectiveness of the dataset, we trained and tested a deep learning model for polyp classification, achieving an accuracy of 96.4%.  We believe that this dataset and our results will contribute to the advancement of automated systems for polyp classification and adenoma abnormality grading.

This research develops an adaptive finite element method to solve time-harmonic acoustic scattering problems, where the incident wave interacts with an object of finite size. The approach employs a hybrid time-domain formulation and a local boundary integral operator to enhance computational efficiency. By utilizing a specific approximation for the scattered wave outside the scatterer, the method significantly reduces memory usage and computational costs associated with the boundary integral equation. The efficiency of the method is further improved through the use of fast solvers and boundary element techniques, which are particularly effective in solving high-frequency problems. The method's performance is demonstrated through numerical experiments, which show that an adaptive approach outperforms non-adaptive methods by reducing the number of degrees of freedom required to achieve a given level of accuracy.

The prevailing theory of planet formation involves the gradual growth of planets through the accumulation of planetesimals in a process that is thought to be an accretion process characterized by low energy levels. Using the algebraic Bethe ansatz, we derive expressions for the form factors of the higher-spin XXZ quantum spin chain's integrable operators, taking the affine quantum-group symmetry into account. By leveraging this symmetry, we can isolate the contributions of individual irreducible representations of the affine quantum group U_q(ĥsl^+2) within the Hilbert space. This allows us to derive the non-trivial analytic properties of the form factors' matrix elements between the eigenstates and the algebraic Bethe ansatz-based off-shell states. Specifically, we show that the poles of these form factors correspond to the states generated by the affine quantum-group symmetry's lowering operators.

This paper introduces a novel approach to voice translation that can translate
any language without the need for extensive data. Unlike traditional
machine translation, our method can also translate the speaking style and
tone of the original speaker. We achieve this by leveraging pre-trained
language and speech models, along with a single-shot adaptation to a target
language. Our method, zero-shot voice translation, has been shown to produce
high-quality translations that are both linguistically accurate and natural
sounding.

We derive an enhanced version of the multipolar expansion suitable for electromagnetic wave interactions with inhomogeneous media, applicable to scenarios where the wavelength is comparable to the object's size. This expansion enables precise computation of scattering and optical forces by decomposing the field into distinct modes, bypassing the constraints of the long wavelength approximation. We demonstrate the validity of our approach through numerical simulations of total scattering and optical force in specific geometries, including a spherical object and a waveguide.

the quantum double of a Young-Capelli algebra and a specific algebra with
schur-shifted symmetric expressions, utilizing a Double Extension Theorem.

In this study, we examine the easiest implementation of the scoto-seesaw model, which offers a compelling solution to multiple outstanding issues in particle physics, including neutrino mass generation, Dark Matter (DM) abundance, and the origin of electroweak symmetry breaking. Within this model, we find that type-II see-saw mechanism is responsible for neutrino mass generation, while stable DM is achieved through an inert doublet model, and the top quark condensation accounts for the electroweak symmetry breaking. By applying a simplified effective potential approach, we demonstrate that the DM stability condition can be satisfied even when the neutrino mass scale is close to the electroweak symmetry breaking scale. As a result, we find that the DM annihilation cross section is consistent with the thermal relic density, and the DM-nucleon scattering cross section falls within the detection range of current and upcoming direct DM detection experiments. Furthermore, we find that the easiest scoto-seewaw model can be reconciled with the stability condition of the Higgs potential up to approximately $10^{10}$ GeV.

The hybridization of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals in transition metal oxides is typically minimal due to their spatial separation, but this phenomenon is more pronounced in 4d and 5d electron systems. As a result, the distinct character of these orbitals becomes less pronounced, and their respective energy levels are significantly altered. This study investigates the interplay of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ electrons in 4d and 5d electron systems using a theoretical model and compares the findings with experimental data from angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. The study reveals that the hybridization of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ electrons leads to the formation of new, distinct bands that are not observed in 3d electron systems. The findings have implications for understanding the behavior of correlated electrons in materials with strong $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ hybridization.

We introduce a relative quantum geometry framework for families of varieties that degenerate, specifically for families where the generic member has a smooth structure, but the degenerate members may have singularities. Building upon this framework, we establish a connection between the symplectic structures of the fibers and their deformation properties. This link is explored through the development of relative Hodge theory, which provides tools to study the relationship between these structures. In particular, we establish the existence of a relative mixed Hodge structure and establish the connection between its filtration and the relative Donaldson-Futaki invariant, which plays a key role in understanding the stability of the family.

This research focuses on developing a sophisticated technique for modifying medical
diagnostic images, specifically for detecting and identifying diseases.
Our proposed method, called Illness-Aware Image Editing (IAIE), is designed to
accurately preserve the presence of diseases in medical images while making
desired changes.
The key innovation of our approach is the incorporation of a disease-preserving
module, which utilizes a combination of image generation and classification
networks to generate images that accurately reflect the presence of diseases.
We tested our method on two different datasets, including one for detecting
pneumonia in X-rays of the lungs and another for identifying multiple diseases
in X-rays of the lungs.
Our results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in
maintaining the accuracy of disease detection while making desired modifications
to the images.
Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/ChenXin00/IAIE.

ViDaExpert is a user-friendly software tool that enables multidimensional data visualization and analysis, specifically designed for vector fields. It incorporates visualization techniques such as VDB, streamlines, and isosurfaces, and facilitates data manipulation through filtering, clipping, and adaptive resolution refinement. ViDaExpert is an open-source application that can be customized and extended through a modular architecture and a Python interface, and is particularly useful for scientific research and education in fields like fluid dynamics, electromagnetism, and astrophysics.

This paper introduces a Swift library for computing the Newtonian potential of a function defined on a two-dimensional area, with particular emphasis on a circular domain. The library utilizes a polar coordinate-based integral method, which is then evaluated through either a Monte Carlo or Gaussian quadrature technique. A Swift implementation of this library is optimized for execution on the GPU through the use of Accelerate, enabling efficient calculations on modern processors. The library's performance is benchmarked against existing implementations in C++ and Python, demonstrating significant improvements in computational speed. The results indicate that the library can produce accurate and rapid solutions to a range of problems, including those encountered in astrophysics, electromagnetics, and fluid dynamics. The library's capabilities are further demonstrated through the calculation of the electrostatic potential of a charged disk and the gravitational potential of a rotating disk.
